themes.label: Login fails after update, network errors
themes.summary: Users across iOS and Android report being unable to log in or load the game after a recent update, with screens stuck on "waiting on network," crashes on open, or repeated download prompts that never complete. Many say reinstalling and resetting their phone did not help, and some mention lost progress, missed login streaks, and no response from support. Complaints span many years of reviews, but the most recent ones cluster around the latest version and mention crashes on launch.
themes.recommendation: Pull crash and network-error logs segmented by app version and OS (especially the latest iOS and Android builds in the 4.5 and 10.3 lines), reproduce the launch-time crash and asset-download failure on Wi-Fi and mobile data, and check whether the server maintenance message is firing incorrectly for updated clients.

themes.label: Grind and pay-to-win progression
themes.summary: Long-time players describe a game that is fun and addictive but increasingly gated behind grinding and real-money spending, with free players unable to keep up with top cards or event tiers. Several say the season reset strips away their hard-earned top cards and leaves them at the bottom, while others complain about rising pack prices and time-gated rewards.
themes.recommendation: Audit progression data for free versus paying players (card tier, event placement, and time-to-tier by season) and prototype a season carry-over or guaranteed top-tier card grant at season start to test whether it reduces churn among F2P users.

themes.label: Pay-to-win monetization and paywalls
themes.summary: Users across Android and iOS say the game has shifted toward requiring real-money spending to get top-tier cards, events, and competitive results, with free and occasional players falling behind. Many point to pack odds, credit-only specialty cards, and event cards hidden behind paywalls, and some say the power gap widened in recent seasons. A few reviewers note they still enjoy the game but feel pushed to spend.
themes.recommendation: Pull pack and event drop-rate data split by spender and free-to-play cohorts for the last three seasons, and evaluate whether tier-card pull rates in low-priced packs and event rewards can be raised for non-paying players.

themes.label: Survivor mode timing and disconnects
themes.summary: Users report that Survivor matches are frustrating because idle or slow opponents let the card-pick timer run down, causing auto-picks, rushed rounds, and long waits of 10 to 15 minutes for other players to finish. Several also describe network errors and cards changing unexpectedly on the draft board, and some say this has cost them finals. The complaints span multiple app versions and both Android and iOS, pointing to a recurring matchmaking and timer problem rather than a single release.
themes.recommendation: Instrument Survivor round timers and wait times by platform and app version, then investigate why auto-pick fires early or late and why rounds stall waiting on other players, shipping a fix with a bounded per-round wait and a clear turn-advance rule.

themes.label: Praise: fun for WWE fans
themes.summary: Users in this cluster mostly praise the game as fun, addictive, and a great pick for WWE fans, with many calling it the best WWE mobile game. The main requests are a card trading system, a wider pool of pullable wrestlers instead of only current WWE roster members, and fewer server disconnects and loading stalls. Several reviewers also say the free-to-play model without forced spending is a major reason they keep playing.
themes.recommendation: Scope a card trading feature as a tracked product request, since it is the most repeated ask in this cluster, and protect the no-forced-spend free-to-play progression when designing it.

themes.label: Praise: addictive, fun gameplay
themes.summary: Users in this cluster are overwhelmingly positive, calling the game awesome, amazing, fun, and addictive, and many say they play it constantly or use it to pass time. A few reviews mention support staff being quick to respond, and one notes the game is too finicky with the internet, but the dominant message is general enthusiasm with no specific feature request. The reviews are short and generic, so they give little detail about which mechanics drive the enjoyment.
themes.recommendation: Protect the core engagement loop in the next release, and run a quick survey or tag analysis of praise to identify which mechanics users cite most so the team knows what to build on.

themes.label: Request to restore NHL SuperCard
themes.summary: Most reviews in this cluster ask the developer to bring back the NHL (and some NBA) SuperCard spin-off, which users say they loved and miss, with several comparing it favorably to the WWE version. The requests span many years and app versions on iOS, suggesting a long-running demand rather than a reaction to a single update.
themes.recommendation: Pull the reviews mentioning NHL, NBA, and 2K SuperCard into a tracked feature-request list, and have the product team check with the 2K licensing and publishing side whether a revived sports SuperCard title or a WWE-adjacent alternative is feasible, then report back on the decision.

themes.label: Request: player-to-player card trading
themes.summary: Users across both iOS and Android repeatedly ask for a trading system so they can swap or donate cards with friends, teammates, or other players, with some suggesting coin or credit sales and team-only trades. The request has persisted from 2017 through 2025, and several reviewers frame trading as the one feature that would make an otherwise well-rated game complete.
themes.recommendation: Scope a discovery study on trade mechanics (team-only versus global, one-for-one versus sell-for-currency, daily or monthly trade limits) by surveying players who have made this request, and use the results to write a prioritized trading feature spec with anti-exploit safeguards.
